title: Shoot
subtitle: 本課只處理 shoot = 用槍射擊／開火 的義項。 不處理攝影（shoot a film）、足球射門、植物長出嫩芽等其他義項。這一組最重要的差異是：只是開火、朝目標射擊、是否擊中
description: 本課只處理 shoot = 用槍射擊／開火 的義項。 不處理攝影（shoot a film）、足球射門、植物長出嫩芽等其他義項。這一組最重要的差異是：只是開火、朝目標射擊、是否擊中、是否受傷、是否死亡，以及正式法律用語。

options.explanation: Fire at ✓ — means discharge a firearm in the direction of a target, whether or not it is hit. Here, the sentence describes shots directed towards a target without stating that they hit. That makes Fire at the most precise wording for this particular meaning of shoot.

Shoot at — means shoot in the direction of a target without necessarily hitting it. This gives directional shooting but does not add the stronger result or formal nuance required here. The decisive clue is that the sentence describes shots directed towards a target without stating that they hit.

Fire — means discharge a firearm and does not itself say whether anyone was hit. This only states that a firearm was discharged and does not tell us whether a person was hit, wounded or killed. The decisive clue is that the sentence describes shots directed towards a target without stating that they hit.

Hit — means strike the target and therefore requires successful contact. This requires successful contact and does not itself say the method was gunfire. The decisive clue is that the sentence describes shots directed towards a target without stating that they hit.

Attack — means act violently against someone or something and is much broader than shooting. This is too broad because an attack can involve many methods other than shooting. The decisive clue is that the sentence describes shots directed towards a target without stating that they hit.

Threaten — means communicate or imply harm and does not require any shooting. A threat may involve no physical action at all, so it cannot replace an actual shooting event. The decisive clue is that the sentence describes shots directed towards a target without stating that they hit.

options.explanation: Gun down — means shoot a person, usually causing them to fall and often implying severe or fatal injury. This is stronger and more dramatic, usually involving a person and severe or fatal consequences. The decisive clue is that the sentence needs a neutral expression that explicitly states the fatal outcome.

Shoot and wound — means shoot someone and cause a non-fatal injury. This requires an explicitly non-fatal injury result. The decisive clue is that the sentence needs a neutral expression that explicitly states the fatal outcome.

Shoot and kill ✓ — means shoot someone and cause their death. Here, the sentence needs a neutral expression that explicitly states the fatal outcome. That makes Shoot and kill the most precise wording for this particular meaning of shoot.

Kill — means cause death and does not specify the method. This gives the fatal result but does not identify shooting as the method. The decisive clue is that the sentence needs a neutral expression that explicitly states the fatal outcome.

Fire — means discharge a firearm and does not itself say whether anyone was hit. This only states that a firearm was discharged and does not tell us whether a person was hit, wounded or killed. The decisive clue is that the sentence needs a neutral expression that explicitly states the fatal outcome.

Attack — means act violently against someone or something and is much broader than shooting. This is too broad because an attack can involve many methods other than shooting. The decisive clue is that the sentence needs a neutral expression that explicitly states the fatal outcome.
